title: No Free Lunch from Random Feature Ensembles: Scaling Laws and Near-Optimality Conditions
summary: Appendix D infers effective-ridge width scaling from P>>N without the necessary ridge regime. A noiseless fixed-ridge example gives a different leading exponent. The checked optimized-risk comparison remains supported.
limitations: No author-code execution or empirical reruns.
No independent validation of imported universality/concentration results.

problems.title: P much larger than N does not alone imply the width-controlled effective ridge

source_claim.location: Section 6.2 Eq.26-27 p.7; Appendix D Eq.D.6 p.24 and first paragraph p.25
source_claim.paraphrase: The separation P>>N forces kappa~N^-alpha, supplying the joint-growth risk exponent.

assumptions: Noiseless,K1,P=N^1.5,lambda1; N can be a square for integral P
Infinite rank, summable spectrum and finite target variance
problems.check: The fixed-point equation implies kappa>=1/P, hence Df1/N=O(N^-1/4)->0, so kappa~1/P=N^-1.5. Since tf1=Df1~pi/(2sqrt(kappa)), Eq12 gives E1~pi/4 N^-0.75, unlike the exponent1 in Eq27.
problems.result: Printed implication and unqualified scaling law fail; independent scalar roots support the asymptotic proof.
counterevidence: A noiseless sufficiently small or optimized ridge interpretation excludes the fixed-ridge example.
Pinned notebook performs a ridge sweep and zero-noise synthetic experiments; Figure4 explicitly optimizes ridge.
No claim of an incorrect optimized-risk exponent or changed benchmark score.
problems.core_dependency: The invalid effective-ridge step feeds D.7-D.12 and the central joint-growth scaling exponent.
problems.impact: Major for the scaling derivation as written, not a refutation of Theorem5.1 or its deterministic-equivalent monotonicity proof.

correction.statement: State and justify a ridge/noise regime, e.g. noiseless P/N->infinity and lambda/(P N^-alpha)->0, or prove entry into it under the intended optimization. Handle noise floors and boundary logarithms explicitly.
